messages.content: Find a picnic spot in Miami.

function.name: local_fauna
function.description: Get information about fauna in a specified region. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The region or area to find information about.

message.content:
Here’s a quick guide to some of the most family‑friendly picnic spots around Miami—complete with what you’ll get there, how easy it is to access, and a few handy “picnic pro” notes: | # | Spot | What Makes It Great | Amenities & Tips | |---|------|---------------------|------------------| | **1** | **South Pointe Park** – *Miami Beach* | • Ocean view + promenade
• Plenty of shaded lawn space
• Close to restaurants & shops | • Restroom facilities
• No grilling allowed (but plenty of benches)
• Parking lots available nearby | | **2** | **Bayfront Park** – Downtown Miami | • Iconic waterfront setting
• Large grassy lawns perfect for blankets
• Kids’ playgrounds | • Public restroom & water fountains
• Grilling not permitted inside park limits
• Good for sunset views | | **3** | **Lummus Park** – South Beach | • Classic beach vibe with boardwalk
• Wide-open sand & grass areas
• Easy beach access | • Portable grill OK only in designated zones
• Handwashing stations near entrance
• Dog leash required outside of pet‑free hours | | **4** | **Oleta River State Park** – North Miami | • Largest urban state park in FL
• Trails, kayak launch, and ample picnic tables
• Natural canopy provides great shade | • Bring your own firewood for campfires (if staying overnight)
• Check seasonal trail closures
• Picnic shelters available during peak season | | **5** | **Crandon Park** – Key Biscayne | • Beautiful sandy shoreline plus lush gardens
• Dedicated picnic pavilion with BBQ grills
• Family fun center & nature trails | • Reserve pavilion ahead via Key Biscayne website
• Dogs welcome but must stay leashed
• Trash cans located throughout | | **6** | **Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park** – Key West (just over 30 miles from Miami) | • Historic lighthouse viewpoint
• Secluded coves ideal for quiet meals
• Well-maintained picnic tables | • Fire pits available (check permit requirements)
• Water supply limited – bring bottled water
• Sunset photography hotspot | ### Quick Checklist Before You Go | Item | Why It Matters | |------|---------------| | **Portable cooler / insulated bag** | Keeps food fresh even under the tropical sun | | **Trash bags** | Leave no trace policy applies everywhere | | **Sun protection** | Sunscreen, hats, sunglasses, and light clothing | | **Water bottle refill station** | Many parks have public taps; keep hydrated | | **First aid kit** | Minor cuts or insect bites may happen | | **Map/phone GPS** | Some parks lack cell service; navigation helps avoid getting lost | #### Pro Tip If you’re planning a larger gathering, call ahead to reserve a pavilion or confirm whether grills are permitted. For example, **Crandon Park** requires reservations for its main pavilion, while **Bayfront Park** has free-use spaces but no built-in grills. Enjoy your sunny day out! If you'd like directions or more details on any specific location, just let me know.
